payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
node.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order. Interpret their reported findings, not merely execution statuses. Complete requires established edited paper-and-cup identity, positive cup-entry evidence, and established completed stuffing from s2. Partial requires positively established requested entry or intermediate stuffing into a cup together with affirmative incompleteness from s2. Absent requires affirmative exclusion of requested progress: established wholly external placement, established rim-only placement without stuffing action, or adequately visible absence of a required object, corroborated or explicitly reconciled by s2. Unresolved candidate identity does not defeat absent if grounded spatial evidence independently excludes entry into any receiver, but identity uncertainty and missing positive cues cannot supply that exclusion. Unknown applies whenever a fact necessary for the applicable conclusion remains unresolved or conflicting observations lack grounded reconciliation. A pass on s1 or the nested boundary-mapping check supplies assessed evidence only; neither earns requested progress or completion credit. A mapping pass with unresolved entry must remain unresolved unless s2 independently supplies the missing grounded finding. Failure of completion alone never establishes absent. Dependent agreement is not independent confirmation. Infer no new visual facts.

dependencies.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible beside a blue, tapered cylindrical receiving object with a broad circular rim/opening, consistent with a cup; the paper overlaps part of its left side. Edited: a blue-and-white printed paper/card is clearly visible, held in a hand, with its boundaries mostly visible. Behind it is a reddish rounded object with a curved outline and a dark line across it; the paper obscures much of this object, and the visible features do not establish that it is a cup. The edited image therefore permits an inventory, but source-to-edit correspondence for the receiving object is unresolved: the edited object does not visibly match the source cup’s blue color or broad rim, and the obscured regions prevent a definitive comparison. No insertion is established by these observations.

Boundary map: The blue-and-white paper/card has a visible upper edge running from the hand-held upper-left area toward a pointed upper-right corner, a right slanted edge descending to a lower-right corner, a lower edge returning toward the lower-left point, and a visible left slanted edge. The hand occludes portions of the upper-left boundary and the paper’s left/central area; the visible endpoints do not establish hidden geometry there. The paper’s right edge and lower-right corner lie in front of the reddish rounded object, whose curved outline and dark line remain visible to the right and below the paper. This establishes local foreground overlap over that object, not paper entry. No visible paper segment disappears behind a receiver boundary; the visible paper edges remain external to the reddish object. The reddish object’s visible structure does not establish a cup, and no alternative receiver is established. Receiver identity: unresolved. Geometry: established wholly external placement relative to the visible candidate object. Requested progress: excluded, because no cup entry is established and the visible paper is outside the candidate object. Completion: excluded. The source cup is blue with a broad circular opening, unlike the edited image’s visible reddish object; correspondence is unresolved.
